newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPAIN SAYS JULY CPI SHOWS REFORMS STILL NEEDED.
newsitem.headline: SPAIN SAYS JULY CPI SHOWS REFORMS STILL NEEDED.

text.p: Spanish inflation data, which was steady at 1.6 percent year-on-year in July, showed that the prices of services are still the most inflationary element and that more reforms are necessary, the Economy Ministry said on Wednesday.

"Services are still the most inflationary component, which shows the need to continue with the deregulation process already started, as well as that wage rises are adjusting to a greater extent than at present to the new framework of low inflation and growing competition," it said.
Services, excluding rents, rose 0.7 percent from June for a 3.7 percent rise year-on-year.
But the July data also showed that Spain is on target to easily meet its 2.2 percent year-end goal for the consumer price index (CPI), the ministry said in a statement.

"July CPI shows a moderate inflation rate which, furthermore, is compatible with the pressure being exerted by the private consumption recovery and the negative impact of the rise in the dollar," the ministry said.
